author: TEDx Talks
description:
How children get to school tells us a lot about the communities we’ve built and whether those communities are serving kids or letting them down. In this talk, educator and Bike Bus World founder Sam Balto shares how walking school buses and bike buses help students arrive at school safer, calmer, more connected, and ready to learn. What began as a simple way to get kids moving became a global movement for active transportation, safer streets, and childhood independence. When communities are safe enough for children to walk and bike to school, they become better for everyone. 

Sam Balto, creator of the Bike Bus, builds community and gets kids moving through collaborations ranging from Stranger Things to rides with Justin Timberlake, Benson Boone, and former U.S. Secretary of Transportation Pete Buttigieg. 

This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: I’m helping kids bike to school—here’s why | Sam Balto | TEDxPortland

author: TEDx Talks
description:
At eleven years old, I believed my future was already written on a badminton court. Years of training, discipline, and dreams pointed in one direction, until a career-changing injury forced me to step away from the sport I loved. What felt like the end of everything I had built became the beginning of something far more meaningful than I could have ever imagined.
In this talk, I share how losing a dream taught me lessons that winning never could. Through moments of disappointment, self-discovery, and resilience, I explore how setbacks often reveal strengths we never knew we had. Sometimes, the paths we never planned lead us to the people we become.
“The Court I Never Returned To” is not just about sports or failure; it is about redefining ambition, embracing change, and understanding that our identity is not limited to a single dream. It is a reminder that ambition is most powerful when guided by awareness, and that our greatest strength lies not in avoiding life's unexpected turns, b
title: The court I never returned to | Shriya Kharade | TEDxThe Orchid School

author: TEDx Talks
description:
The Quiet Things We Leave Behind is a deeply personal talk about how the smallest everyday moments often have the greatest impact on the people around us. Through three true stories from my own life, I explore how ordinary conversations, missed opportunities, and unspoken words can shape relationships far more than dramatic events ever do.

The first story reflects on a simple argument with my mother that taught me how deeply our words can affect the people closest to us. The second recounts my experience with a German exchange student, showing how regret can become a powerful teacher and inspire us to value every new relationship. The final story examines a friendship that slowly faded through silence, revealing the importance of honest communication before distance becomes permanent.

Rather than focusing on grand acts of kindness, this talk encourages audiences to pay attention to the quiet choices they make every day—how they speak, listen, apologise, and show up for others. It is
title: The Quiet Things We Leave Behind | Ranbir Singh | TEDxThe Orchid School

author: TEDx Talks
description: Dr. Douglas Hilbert argues that living longer only matters if we can stay healthy, active and fulfilled. Drawing from his experience as a doctor and his own struggles, he highlights three principles: make time for your health, recognize how relationships shape your habits, and advocate for yourself. Simple choices can prevent disease, while intentional goals and difficult conversations can help break unhealthy patterns. Ultimately, Dr. Hilbert encourages us to take control of our health and relationships so we can “die young as late as possible”—living not just longer, but better Dr. Douglas Hilbert is a board-certified Internal Medicine physician, founder of HilbertMD, and Fellow of the American College of Physicians. He founded the first Academic Hospitalist program in the US Department of Defense at Brooke Army Medical Center. His work centers on helping people live stronger, longer, and with greater purpose, grounded in resilience, discipline, and the belief that we are capable of
title: Die young as late as possible | Dr Douglas Hilbert | TEDxCambridge University

description: From melancholy to new beginnings, Jo Nara brings two emotional worlds to the TEDx stage. With “New Dawn” and “Gspüt's Gfüh,” the Austrian singer-songwriter explores inner strength, self-love, and the emotions that stay with us when words alone are not enough. Jo Nara creates intimate Alternative Pop about finding oneself in a noisy world. Combining soulful piano and bilingual lyrics (English/Austrian Dialect), the half-Filipino artist delivers a warm, decelerated sound; authentic, moving, and uniquely his own. author: TEDx Talks
description:
Fear rarely arrives with a warning. It settles quietly, laying one brick at a time until the walls around us feel like home. In this deeply personal talk, I reflect on how a childhood experience with fear slowly expanded into social anxiety, silence, and the habit of shrinking myself to fit the expectations of others.

But the greatest realization wasn’t that fear had trapped me—it was that I had unknowingly handed it the blueprint. The stories we repeatedly tell ourselves eventually become the walls we live within, and the voices we hear long enough often begin to sound like our own.

Through humor, vulnerability, and honest reflection, I explore why courage is not the disappearance of fear but the decision to stop letting it author our identity. Growth begins the moment we question the narratives that have quietly governed our lives and choose authenticity over approval.

This talk is an invitation to examine the invisible architecture each of us carries, to reclaim the spaces fear
title: The Walls We Carry | Adwitya Choudhari | TEDxThe Orchid School

author: TEDx Talks
description: Life, like sports, brings sudden, unpredictable shifts when rules change or plans fail. The author calls these moments "The Turn"—times of deep uncertainty, such as facing a failed exam, losing a spot on a team, or encountering sudden technology shifts.  While ordinary people complain and resist disruption, true champions adapt. In sports, top athletes used sudden changes like the Decision Review System (DRS) in cricket and Hawk-Eye in tennis not as frustrations, but as tactical tools to gain an advantage. Similarly, when the speaker  transitioned from playing keyboard to learning guitar, initial pain and frustration were overcome by adapting existing music knowledge and embracing the discomfort.  Ultimately, success does not belong to the strongest, but to those who adapt first. Instead of complaining about unfair setbacks, champions look for solutions, using every failure, rejection, and disruption as fuel to build resilience and come out stronger. author: TEDx Talks
description:
Learning and doing the right thing is important, but perhaps even more important is understanding why we choose to do it. In today’s world of instant gratification and constant recognition, understanding and applying our ancient wisdom has never been more crucial.

In his first TEDx Talk, Nimit shares his journey of understanding the shlok from Bhagvad Gita:
‘Karmanye vadhikaraste ma phaleshu kadachana’; a teaching that encourages us to focus on our
actions rather than their outcomes. He relates this simple yet difficult to apply shlok from the fresh
lens and life of 10-year old school boy. Blending storytelling, humor, and practical insights, Nimit also introduces a simple three-step approach that anyone can use to practice this timeless principle in everyday life. Nimit, a 10-years-old student of Grade 5, is a happy and playful child. He is friendly, caring, and loves spending time with his friends and family. His helpful nature, and ability to sense how others feel, helps him build
title: Going Beyond Rewards | Nimit Panwalkar | TEDxThe Orchid School

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In this talk, Dr. Amit Samarth shares his experiences as an endurance athlete and explains that training can never fully prepare us for the challenges of real life. The actual test is often harder and more unpredictable than we expect. Through his experiences, he shows that we don’t need a perfect plan or to feel completely ready before taking on something difficult. Success comes from taking action, adapting to challenges, and continuing forward even when we are not ready. Dr. Amit Samarth is a physician, public health professional, and ultra-endurance cyclist. He holds an MBBS from Indira Gandhi Medical College, Nagpur, and a Master’s in Public Health from Johns Hopkins University, USA.

He has completed some of the world’s toughest endurance races, including the 9,100 km Red Bull Trans-Siberian Extreme and the 4,900 km Race Across America. In 2024, he secured 1st place in Race Across India, covering 3,758 km from Srinagar to Kanyakumari. In 2023, he won Race Across India Solo and s
title: We Are Never Ready? Ghostrider | Dr. Amit Samarth | TEDxThe Orchid School

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In my talk, I share how one small decision changed the way I saw myself. I used to be afraid of speaking on stage and always hoped I wouldn’t be chosen for performances or speaking roles. Then one day, my teacher gave me an important role in our class concert. I was scared and wanted to say no, but I decided to give it a try.

That experience taught me that courage comes before confidence. I didn’t become confident first and then perform; I became confident because I chose to perform despite being afraid.

I believe everyone has their own “stage.” It may not be a real stage—it could be answering a question in class, trying a new sport, making a new friend, or taking on any challenge that feels scary. My message is that we should not let fear make our decisions. Sometimes, one small brave step is all it takes to discover what we are truly capable of and to turn our own lives in a new direction. Siya is a 9-year-old student who believes that every challenge is an opportunity to grow. Cu
title: What Is Your Stage? | Siya Prayag | TEDxThe Orchid School

author: TEDx Talks
description:
My talk uses an unusual teacher: slime mould, a brainless organism that, when researchers placed food sources on a map of Tokyo, grew a network almost identical to the city's railway system. I use this to explore how we actually make progress in life. We tend to misunderstand our own lives by treating them as completed stories, chasing five-year plans and grand purposes, when most of life is really lived at the next turn, not viewed from above.

I trace this through three moments from my own life. A seventh-grade river cleanup where I felt crushed by the scale of pollution I couldn't fix, which created a thinking pattern of zooming out onto the entire problem instead of the step in front of me. A grade 10 competition where I was doing both a national science competition and preparing for board exams, and the fear of falling behind brought that same zoomed-out thinking rushing back, this time one I could recognise as it happened. And the moment I picked a stream of study, Science, Comm
title: The Sum of Small Decisions | Riyana Hatkar | TEDxThe Orchid School

description:
Life can take unexpected turns and sometimes things may not go the way we want. This talk shares simple and funny stories about running, failure, friendship, and growing a plant to show that we should not give up when things get difficult. Instead, we should learn from our experiences, try again, and keep moving forward. When life takes a turn, we should “turn the turn” and make the best of it. description: This talk uses baking as a way to explain how our experiences shape who we become. It shows that failure, patience, hard work, and consistency are important parts of growing. Just like batter needs time to rise, we also need time and challenges to learn and become stronger. The talk reminds us that the journey is just as important as the final result. She enjoys baking, spending time in nature, working with children, and embracing opportunities that help her grow, whether through speaking at TEDx, leading projects, or learning something new. author: TEDx Talks
description: This talk explores the pressure to become one fixed version of ourselves in a world full of labels, expectations, and ideas of perfection. It shows that having different sides, changing our minds, and being full of contradictions are not flaws, but a natural part of growing and discovering who we are. Instead of trying to fit into one perfect identity, we are encouraged to accept and celebrate the many different versions of ourselves. Tanisha Badigannavar believes curiosity is more valuable than certainty. A 17-year-old student with interests in psychology, philosophy, and human behaviour, she is fascinated by the contradictions that make people who they are. Alongside serving as the Senior House Captain, she enjoys writing, creating podcasts, and exploring ideas that sit at the intersection of identity, behaviour, and storytelling. Her TEDx talk, The Versions Within the Mess, reflects that curiosity, exploring why our complexity is not something to overcome, but something to embrace.
title: The Versions Within the Mess | Tanisha Badigannavar | TEDxThe Orchid School

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Perché un accordo sospeso ci mette in tensione? Perché una melodia che conosciamo ci dà piacere? E perché una nota “sbagliata” può catturare immediatamente la nostra attenzione? Attraverso musica, neuroscienze e psicologia, questo talk esplora il modo in cui il nostro cervello costruisce aspettative, reagisce agli errori e impara. Un viaggio alla scoperta della musica come palestra per la mente e un invito a non lasciare che sia l’algoritmo a decidere cosa ascoltare.

description:

Un invito ad agire, osare e dare una possibilità alla fortuna.

It also shows why there’s a growing need for more inclusive representation and acceptance of different body types and appearances.

 Magathi Narayanan is a third-year Electronics and Communication Engineering student at Chennai Institute of Technology who believes that words and voices can shape society and spark meaningful change. title: Social Death of Unesthetic Women | Magathi Narayanan | TEDxChennai Institute of Technology Women

What if waiting until you’re ready is the very thing keeping you from becoming who you’re meant to be?

Film director and entrepreneur Director Pink shares her unconventional journey from making shoes and bags at 14 to becoming a graphic designer, animator, radio presenter, filmmaker, entrepreneur and founder of Pinkline Academy. Director Pink challenges the idea that we need perfect clarity before taking action. Instead, she argues that clarity comes because of movement, we discover ourselves, our skills and our direction by doing, experimenting and refusing to stand still.

Whether you're a student, creative, entrepreneur or simply figuring out your next step, this talk is a reminder that you don't have to be the best before you begin. You just need to start. description:
In a world where “African” is often reduced to patterns, colours, cowries and other familiar visual symbols, Chukwu Adeze Victoria challenges creators to look beyond the surface. She explores African identity as a system of meaning rooted in language, rhythm, storytelling, symbols, context and lived experience.

Through examples from African proverbs, Igbo Uli and traditional stories, she shows how creators can move from simply transferring African visuals to truly translating culture into meaningful creative work. She calls on writers, designers, architects, storytellers and other creatives to engage with culture, understand its context and create from deeper cultural knowledge.

The message is simple: Africa is not a pattern. It is meaning, culture and depth. Chukwu Adaeze Victoria doesn't just design brands, she builds legacies with pixels and purpose.
